problem.title: Hundreds of applications. One afternoon to read them.
problem.body: A single job post can draw hundreds of applications. Recruiters skim, get tired, and good candidates fall through. Generic AI screeners hand back a number nobody can explain, which is worse. You can't defend it to a hiring manager, or to a candidate who asks why.

how.title: Four steps, and the first one is a forwarding rule.
how.lede: Nothing changes for your candidates, and nothing changes about where they apply.
how.s1Body: Your organization gets a private email alias. Point your careers inbox at it with a forwarding rule. No mailbox OAuth, no integration project, no change to where candidates apply.
how.s2Body: PDFs, Word documents, even scanned CVs. The agent reads them visually when there is no text layer, and extracts skills, work history with dates, education, certifications and contact details into structured fields.
how.s3Body: You define what the role requires: must-haves as a hard gate, nice-to-haves with weights. The agent judges each requirement on its own and writes a sentence of evidence for it.
how.s4Body: Filter by score, university, nationality, referral or review flags. Open any candidate to see the full breakdown: which requirements they met, which they missed, and why.
how.shotDesc: A candidate's score, with the evidence behind every requirement
how.shotAlt: A candidate's score panel in Staffly ATS+ showing 71 out of 100 and a note that the candidate meets every mandatory requirement, followed by a written rationale and each mandatory requirement checked off with a sentence of evidence drawn from the resume.

why.title: A score you can put in front of a hiring manager.
why.lede: Every number on this page traces back to a requirement you wrote and a sentence of evidence the agent found in the resume.
why.explainBody: The AI decides met or not met and writes the rationale. The score itself is computed by deterministic code from those verdicts. The model never sees the formula and is never asked for a number.
why.explainCaption: So a score reads like this, rather than “the AI said 78.”
why.inventBody: If a resume does not state something, the field comes back empty. Nationality is recorded only when it is written outright, never guessed from a name, a language, a location or a phone number.
why.fairBody: Candidates are judged only against the requirements you wrote. Protected characteristics are excluded from the evaluation, and the scoring agent is never shown the candidate's nationality at all.
why.hardenBody: A resume is a document a stranger emailed you, and it can carry hidden text aimed at the AI. Staffly treats every resume as untrusted input, and the scoring step reads structured fields rather than raw document text. A candidate can't talk their way into a 95.
why.flagTitle: It flags what needs a human
why.flagBody: A candidate who misses one hard requirement out of four. A borderline score that only cleared the bar because of a referral. Anything the model couldn't judge. These surface for review instead of being rejected quietly.
why.tenantBody: Every organization's data is separated at the database level. Resumes live in private storage behind short-lived signed links, and candidate files are deleted with the account.

faq.title: Before you ask.
faq.q1: What happens to our candidate data?
faq.a1: Each organization's records are separated at the database level, so no other tenant can reach them. Resumes are held in private storage and are only ever served through short-lived signed links. When you close your account, candidate files are deleted with it.
faq.a2: No. Staffly reads and ranks so you can spend your time on the people worth a conversation. Every score comes with the evidence behind it, and anything borderline is flagged for a human rather than rejected quietly. The hiring decision stays yours.
faq.q3: What file types does it handle?
faq.a3: PDFs and Word documents, including scanned CVs with no text layer. Those are read visually rather than parsed as text, so a photographed or scanned resume is still extracted and scored.
faq.q4: Can a candidate manipulate their score?
faq.a4: Resumes are treated as untrusted input, so hidden instructions aimed at the AI are not followed. The scoring step reads the structured fields extracted from the resume rather than the raw document text, which leaves nothing for a candidate to write into.
faq.q5: How does it connect to the way we hire today?
faq.a5: You add a forwarding rule to your careers inbox pointing at the private alias we give you. There is no mailbox OAuth and no integration project, and candidates keep applying exactly where they do now.
faq.a6: Nationality is recorded only when a resume states it outright, and it is never inferred from a name, a language, a location or a phone number. The scoring agent is never shown it. It exists as a filter for your own review, not as an input to the score.
faq.a7: No. Seats are unlimited on every plan, so you can invite your whole team, including hiring managers who only need to look at a shortlist. Billing is based on the number of applications screened, not on how many people log in.
